name: AIS: vessel positions
description: SIGNAL-015 (baseline): ITU-R M.1371 AIS Class A position reports on the two fixed international marine VHF channels, AIS1/Ch87B 161.975 MHz and AIS2/Ch88B 162.025 MHz (followed together, not discovered by hopping — the channel plan is fixed by treaty, unlike a pager net's unknown channel count). GMSK at 9600 Bd, h = 0.5 (deviation = rate/4, BT = 0.4 on air but the receive-side discriminator is the same non-coherent MSK chain as `msk_demod` uses elsewhere), NRZI line coding (0 = transition, ISO/IEC 13239 §4.4.1, the `nrzi` default), then standard HDLC framing (ITU-R M.1371-5 Annex 2, ISO/IEC 13239): the 0x7E flags are found on the still-stuffed line (stuffing guarantees six ones in a row occur only in a flag there; destuffed data can contain 01111110, so searching after destuffing would cut frames short), each variable-length frame ended by (and, per `sync_search`'s terminator convention, including) the next 0x7E; each frame is then zero-bit destuffed on its own (T-613's `bitstuff` in frames mode: the rule restarts per frame, and the closing flag's six ones pass through) and its octets reassembled LSB first (`bit_order: lsb` — HDLC sends every octet LSB first, and the FCS low-order octet first). The `crc` node's `end_trim_bits: 8` excludes the trailing flag octet from the FCS = CRC-16/X-25 a.k.a. CRC-16/IBM-SDLC (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, refin/refout, xorout 0xFFFF, check field little-endian) computation and check-field lookup, and its stripped output leaves the flag bits as harmless trailing padding past the fields the field map defines. The frame's payload is decoded for the common navigation block shared by message types 1/2/3 (Class A position report): MMSI, navigational status, speed/course/heading over ground, longitude/latitude (1/600000 minute resolution) and timestamp. Other message types (5 static/voyage data, 18/19 Class B, 24 static data report, …) are carried as raw frames only — their own field maps are a follow-up. Oracle: py/fixtures/ais_ref.py (T-963), validated against the `ais_vessels` synthetic scene.

nodes.label: 0x7E … 0x7E on the stuffed line (the flag is unique only before destuffing)
Remove zero-stuffing per frame; octets LSB first
FCS: CRC-16/X-25 (the terminator flag is part of the frame; end_trim_bits skips it)

ais_position_report.description: One HDLC frame's data (FCS already stripped), MSB first. `message_type` and `mmsi` are common to every AIS message; the rest of the common navigation block (ITU-R M.1371 §3.3.1) is decoded for types 1/2/3 (Class A position report) only.
